entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lucius Annaeus Cornutus, a Stoic philosopher, flourished in Rome during the reign of Nero (54-68 CE). His house served as a school of philosophy, attracting prominent figures like Epictetus.

Born in the 1st century CE, Cornutus' life is not well-documented, but his philosophical contributions were significant.

His teachings emphasized the importance of reason, self-control, and the interconnectedness of all things.

The legacy of Lucius Annaeus Cornutus can be seen in the continued influence of Stoicism on Western philosophy.

'Wisdom is the life of the soul,' Cornutus once said, highlighting the enduring importance of his ideas.
